conceptual assets.information: The accumulated cycle count used to report cycle and machine-cycle CSR values. It enters through the CSR control record when software writes the counter and leaves through the CSR read-data output.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is at risk because the cycle counter value reaches the externally visible rdata_o through cycle_rd at lines 136 and 97. Integrity is at risk because csr_wdata is wired to cycle_inst at line 135 and the counter stores it at lines 303 and 326. Expected behavior can be undermined because cpu_debug and cnt_halt suppress cnt_en at line 108, which drives the cycle counter increment at line 131 and can produce an incorrect count.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could read the cycle count through rdata_o, overwrite it through a CSR write, or force debug or halt control so that counting is suppressed.

conceptual assets.information: The accumulated number of retired instructions used to report the instruction-retirement CSR values. It enters through the CSR control record for software writes and leaves through the CSR read-data output.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is at risk because the instruction-retirement value reaches rdata_o through instret_rd at lines 155 and 97. Integrity is at risk because csr_wdata is wired to instret_inst at line 154 and the counter stores it at lines 303 and 326. Expected behavior can be undermined because cpu_debug and cnt_halt suppress cnt_en at line 110, which drives the instruction-retirement counter increment at line 150 and can produce an incorrect count.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could read or overwrite the retirement count through the CSR path, or assert debug or halt control to make the reported instruction count inaccurate.

conceptual assets.information: The per-event performance-monitoring counts used to measure selected processor events. They enter through the CSR control record for counter writes and leave through the merged CSR read-data output.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Confidentiality is at risk because hpmcnt values flow through hpm_read_back at lines 190 and 222-227 and then reach rdata_o at line 97. Integrity is at risk because csr_wdata is wired to each HPM counter at line 189 and the counter registers accept it at lines 303 and 326. Expected behavior can be undermined because cpu_debug, cnt_halt and event selection determine cnt_en at line 112, which drives HPM counter increments at line 185 and can cause incorrect measurements.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could read or overwrite performance counts through the CSR interface, or manipulate debug, halt or event controls to suppress or distort measurements.

conceptual assets.information: The per-counter event-selection settings stored in hpmevent determine which processor events increment the hardware performance-monitoring counters. The settings enter through the CSR control record and can be returned through the CSR read-data output.
conceptual assets.rubric reason: Integrity is at risk because a CSR write condition at line 199 stores csr_wdata into hpmevent at line 200, allowing the selected event set to be changed.
conceptual assets.attack: An attacker could issue an unauthorized CSR write to replace an HPM event selector and make the counters report different events.

considered, not kept.reason: csr_addr, csr_re and csr_we are access command fields that select and qualify accesses to the kept counter and configuration information, so Access command fields makes them part of those accesses rather than separate information.
cnt_en is an internal increment pulse that only paces the counter updates through lines 108-112, 131, 150 and 185, so the Pacing pulses rule folds it into the counter information.
time_rd is assigned only zero constants at lines 140 and 163-164, so the RTL holds no time-counter information requiring a security objective.
